question: Which ISRO centre, located in Bengaluru, is primarily responsible for the design, development and building of satellites?
solution_text:
The correct answer is U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC), located in Bengaluru, is the ISRO centre primarily responsible for the design, development, fabrication and testing of satellites. (यू आर राव उपग्रह केंद्र — उपग्रह निर्माण)

 

• It was earlier known as the ISRO Satellite Centre (ISAC) and was renamed after the noted space scientist Prof. Udupi Ramachandra Rao.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — major ISRO centres)

 

• Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC), Thiruvananthapuram - designs and develops launch vehicles (rockets).

 

• Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), Sriharikota - the main launch/spaceport of ISRO.

 

• Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC) - develops liquid propulsion stages.

 

• ISRO's headquarters are in Bengaluru; ISRO was founded in 1969, and Dr. Vikram Sarabhai is regarded as the father of the Indian space programme.

 

NOTE

 

• The Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) in Ahmedabad is a research institute for space and allied sciences.

question: The 'Startup India' initiative, aimed at promoting startups and entrepreneurship, was launched by the Government of India in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2016.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Startup India' initiative was launched by the Government of India on 16 January 2016. It aims to build a strong ecosystem for nurturing innovation and startups in the country, so as to drive economic growth and create employment. (स्टार्टअप इंडिया — 2016)

 

• Key benefits under the initiative include tax exemptions, easier compliance, funding support (through the Fund of Funds and the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme) and simplified processes for startups.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — related initiatives)

 

• Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) - promotes innovation through Atal Tinkering Labs (ATLs) in schools and Atal Incubation Centres.

 

• Make in India (2014) - aims to make India a global manufacturing hub.

 

• Digital India (2015) - aims to transform India into a digitally empowered society.

 

NOTE

 

• 16 January is now observed as 'National Startup Day'. India has one of the largest startup ecosystems in the world, with many 'unicorns' (startups valued at over one billion dollars).

question: Who played the most significant role in integrating over 500 princely states into the Indian Union after independence in 1947?
option_3: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Kalam'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/Kalam.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, as the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of independent India, played the most significant role in integrating over 500 princely states into the Indian Union. (सरदार वल्लभभाई पटेल — रियासतों का एकीकरण)

 

• He was ably assisted by V. P. Menon (the Secretary of the States Department). For his role in unifying the country, Patel is known as the 'Iron Man of India' and the 'Bismarck of India'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

 

• Most princely states signed the 'Instrument of Accession' to join India. States such as Junagadh, Hyderabad and Jammu & Kashmir required special efforts.

 

• Sardar Patel's birthday, 31 October, is observed as 'National Unity Day' (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas). The 'Statue of Unity' in Gujarat, the tallest statue in the world, is dedicated to him.

 

NOTE

 

• The princely states were given three options at the time of independence: join India, join Pakistan, or remain independent.

question: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 - one of the three new criminal laws - replaced which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Indian Penal Code, 1860.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860. It is the new law that defines various crimes and their punishments in India. (भारतीय न्याय संहिता — भारतीय दंड संहिता, 1860 का स्थान)

 

• The BNS was introduced as part of the effort to modernise and 'decolonise' India's criminal justice system. It introduces new offences such as organized crime, terrorism, mob lynching and community service as a punishment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — the three new criminal laws, in force 1 July 2024)

 

• Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 - replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860.

 

• Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 - replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973.

 

• Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 - replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.

 

NOTE

 

• The Indian Contract Act, 1872 is a civil law and was not replaced by these criminal-law reforms.

question: The 'Bombay High', an important offshore oil field of India, is located in which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Arabian Sea.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Bombay High' (now often called 'Mumbai High') is a major offshore oil field of India, located in the Arabian Sea, about 160 km off the coast of Mumbai. (बॉम्बे हाई — अरब सागर)

 

• It was discovered in the 1970s and is operated by the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC). The oil is extracted using offshore platforms and processed on the mainland.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — oil fields of India)

 

• Onshore oil fields: Digboi, Naharkatiya and Moran-Hugrijan (Assam); Ankleshwar and Kalol (Gujarat).

 

• Offshore oil fields: Bombay High (Arabian Sea) and the Krishna-Godavari basin (Bay of Bengal).

 

• Digboi (Assam) is the site of the oldest oil refinery in India (and Asia).

 

NOTE

 

• The ONGC (Oil and Natural Gas Corporation) is the largest oil and gas exploration and production company in India.

question: In Indian classical music, the term 'Alaap' refers to which of the following?
option_1: The slow, improvised opening section of a raga, without rhythm, that introduces the raga
option_2: A percussion instrument played with the fingers
option_3: A fixed rhythmic cycle of sixteen beats
option_4: A group of seven basic musical notes
solution_text:
The correct answer is The slow, improvised opening section of a raga, without rhythm, that introduces the raga.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Alaap' is the slow, unmetered (without rhythm/percussion) and improvised opening section of a raga performance. In the Alaap, the artist gradually introduces and explores the notes and mood of the raga, before the rhythmic composition begins. (आलाप — राग की धीमी, अलयबद्ध प्रस्तावना)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — terms of Indian classical music)

 

• Raga - a melodic framework (a specific combination of notes).

 

• Taal - the rhythmic cycle (e.g., 'Teentaal' has sixteen beats).

 

• Saptak - the group of seven basic notes (Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni).

 

• Gharana - a school or lineage/style of music.

 

NOTE

 

• After the Alaap, a performance usually moves into the 'Jor' (with a pulse) and then the 'Jhala' (fast section) or a composition with rhythmic accompaniment.

question:
Consider the following statements about the physical features of India:

1. The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass lying to the south of the Narmada river.

2. The Western Ghats are generally higher than the Eastern Ghats.

3. The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest fold mountain ranges in India.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three statements are correct. (भारत की भौतिक विशेषताएँ)

 

• Statement 1 is correct: The Deccan Plateau is a large, triangular plateau lying to the south of the Narmada river, bordered by the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: The Western Ghats (average height 900-1600 m) are generally higher and more continuous than the Eastern Ghats, which are lower and broken by rivers.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: The Aravalli Range in Rajasthan is one of the oldest fold mountain ranges in the world (and in India).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — physical divisions of India)

 

• The physical divisions of India are: the Northern (Himalayan) Mountains, the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands.

 

• Anaimudi (in the Western Ghats, Kerala) is the highest peak of peninsular/South India.

 

NOTE

 

• All three statements are correct, so the answer is '1, 2 and 3'.

question: The Red Fort (Lal Qila) in Delhi, built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, is primarily constructed of which material?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Red sandstone.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Red Fort (Lal Qila) in Delhi is primarily constructed of red sandstone, which gives the fort its name and its distinctive colour. (लाल किला — लाल बलुआ पत्थर)

 

• It was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in the 17th century (completed around 1648), when he shifted the Mughal capital from Agra to Shahjahanabad (Delhi). It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — the Red Fort)

 

• Every year on Independence Day (15 August), the Prime Minister of India hoists the national flag and addresses the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort.

 

• Inside the Red Fort are important structures such as the Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience) and the Diwan-i-Khas (Hall of Private Audience).

 

NOTE

 

• Shah Jahan is also famous for building the Taj Mahal (white marble) at Agra and the Jama Masjid at Delhi.

question: The 'Chapchar Kut', a spring festival celebrated with the Cheraw (bamboo) dance, is an important festival of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Chapchar Kut' is the most important spring festival of Mizoram, celebrated in March after the completion of the most arduous task of the jhum (shifting) cultivation - the clearing of the forest for the new crop. (चापचार कुट — मिज़ोरम)

 

• The highlight of the festival is the famous 'Cheraw' dance (the bamboo dance), in which dancers move nimbly between bamboo staves that are clapped together in rhythm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — festivals of the North-East)

 

• Mizoram - Chapchar Kut.

• Nagaland - Hornbill Festival, Sekrenyi.

• Manipur - Yaoshang, Lai Haraoba.

• Meghalaya - Wangala (Garo), Nongkrem (Khasi).

• Assam - Bihu.

 

NOTE

 

• Chapchar Kut is a celebration of community bonding, and includes songs, dances and traditional games.

question: The 'Great Granary', one of the largest structures of the Indus Valley Civilization, was discovered at which of the following sites?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harappa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A large granary (the 'Great Granary') was discovered at Harappa, one of the most important sites of the Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilization. Granaries were used for the storage of surplus food grains, showing an organised system of collection and distribution. (महान अन्नागार — हड़प्पा)

 

• Harappa is located on the banks of the Ravi river (in present-day Pakistan). The civilization is named after this site, as it was one of the first to be excavated (in 1921, by Daya Ram Sahni).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — Harappan sites and their notable finds)

 

• Mohenjo-daro - the Great Bath, a large granary, the bronze 'Dancing Girl'.

 

• Lothal (Gujarat) - a dockyard (evidence of maritime trade).

 

• Kalibangan (Rajasthan) - ploughed fields and fire altars.

 

• Dholavira (Gujarat) - an advanced water-management system.

 

NOTE

 

• The Indus Valley Civilization (c. 2500 BCE) is famous for its town planning, drainage system and the use of standardised weights and measures.

question: In the traditional Indian sport of Kho-Kho, the players who chase and try to touch the opposing players are called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chasers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the game of Kho-Kho, the team that is 'chasing' has players called 'chasers' (or attackers), who try to touch/tag the players of the opposing team to put them out. The opposing players who try to avoid being touched are called 'runners' (or defenders/dodgers). (खो-खो — चेज़र)

 

• The chasers sit in a row (facing alternate directions) and one active chaser pursues the runners; a chaser can pass the chase to a seated teammate by touching them and saying 'Kho'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

 

• Kho-Kho is one of the oldest traditional (tag) sports of India, along with Kabaddi.

 

• Kho-Kho was included as a competitive/medal event in some recent editions of the National Games, and a Kho-Kho World Cup has also been organised.

 

NOTE

 

• In Kabaddi, the attacking player is called the 'raider' and the defenders are the 'antis' - which is different from the terms used in Kho-Kho.

question: The Cholas of South India were especially famous for their efficient and well-developed system of which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Village (local) self-government.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Cholas were especially famous for their efficient and well-developed system of village (local) self-government. Villages were largely self-governing, managed by local assemblies. (चोल — ग्राम स्वशासन)

 

• The main types of assemblies were the 'Ur' (a general village assembly), the 'Sabha' (an assembly of Brahmin villages / agraharas) and the 'Nagaram' (an assembly of merchants). The famous Uttaramerur inscriptions describe the detailed working and election of members of these assemblies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — the Cholas)

 

• The Cholas reached their peak under Rajaraja Chola I and Rajendra Chola I.

 

• They built magnificent temples (such as the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur) and are famous for their bronze sculptures, especially the image of 'Nataraja' (the dancing Shiva).

 

NOTE

 

• The Chola navy was powerful and undertook overseas expeditions, including to the Srivijaya empire in Southeast Asia.

question:
Consider the following statements about Indian domestic cricket:

Statement 1: The Ranji Trophy is India's premier domestic first-class cricket tournament.

Statement 2: The Duleep Trophy is contested between zonal (regional) teams.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both Statement 1 and Statement 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. (भारतीय घरेलू क्रिकेट)

 

• Statement 1 is correct: The Ranji Trophy is India's premier domestic first-class cricket tournament, contested between teams representing states and regions. It was named after Kumar Shri Ranjitsinhji.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: The Duleep Trophy has traditionally been contested between zonal (regional) teams (such as North Zone, South Zone, etc.). It is named after Kumar Shri Duleepsinhji.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — Indian domestic cricket tournaments)

 

• Ranji Trophy - premier first-class (multi-day) tournament.

 

• Duleep Trophy - first-class tournament (zonal teams).

 

• Vijay Hazare Trophy - domestic one-day (List A) tournament.

 

• Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy - domestic Twenty20 (T20) tournament.

 

• Irani Trophy - played between the Ranji Trophy champions and the Rest of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Both statements are correct, so the answer is 'Both Statement 1 and Statement 2'.

question: The 'Chabahar Port', developed with Indian assistance to boost trade and give India access to Central Asia, is located in which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iran.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chabahar Port is located in Iran, on the Gulf of Oman. India has been developing this port to boost trade and to gain access to Afghanistan and Central Asia, bypassing Pakistan. (चाबहार बंदरगाह — ईरान)

 

• It is strategically important because it gives India a sea-land access route to Afghanistan and Central Asia, and is linked to the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — India's connectivity projects)

 

• Kaladan Multimodal Transit Transport Project - connects India (Kolkata) to Sittwe port in Myanmar and onward to Mizoram.

 

• India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway - connects India to Southeast Asia.

 

NOTE

 

• The Chabahar Port supports India's 'Connect Central Asia' policy and provides an alternative to the Chinese-developed Gwadar Port in Pakistan (which is nearby).

question: Who is the author of the celebrated novel 'A Suitable Boy'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vikram Seth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'A Suitable Boy' (1993) was written by Vikram Seth. It is one of the longest novels ever published in a single volume in English, set in post-independence India, and follows the search for a suitable husband for the young woman Lata. (अ सूटेबल बॉय — विक्रम सेठ)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — authors and their works)

 

• Vikram Seth - 'A Suitable Boy', 'The Golden Gate' (a novel in verse).

 

• Jhumpa Lahiri - 'Interpreter of Maladies' (Pulitzer Prize), 'The Namesake'.

 

• Kiran Desai - 'The Inheritance of Loss' (Booker Prize, 2006).

 

• Arundhati Roy - 'The God of Small Things' (Booker Prize, 1997).

 

NOTE

 

• Vikram Seth's novel 'A Suitable Boy' was adapted into a television series by the BBC.

question: Which of the following correctly describes the term 'birth rate' in demography?
option_1: The number of persons migrating into an area in a year
option_2: The number of live births per 1,000 population in a year
option_3: The total population of a country divided by its area
option_4: The number of deaths per 1,000 population in a year
solution_text:
The correct answer is The number of live births per 1,000 population in a year.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'birth rate' (crude birth rate) is defined as the number of live births per 1,000 population in a year. It is an important indicator used to study the growth of population. (जन्म दर)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — demographic terms)

 

• Death rate (crude death rate) - the number of deaths per 1,000 population in a year.

 

• Natural growth rate of population - the difference between the birth rate and the death rate.

 

• Migration - the movement of people from one place to another; it can be immigration (into an area) or emigration (out of an area).

 

• Population density - the number of persons living per unit area (per square kilometre).

 

NOTE

 

• When the birth rate and the death rate become nearly equal, the population tends to become stable (population stabilization).

question: Which of the following correctly describes the position of the National Security Advisor (NSA) of India?
option_1: A constitutional post specified in the Constitution, with a fixed six-year term
option_2: The presiding officer of the Rajya Sabha
option_3: The chief adviser to the Prime Minister on matters of national security and strategic affairs
option_4: The head of the Supreme Court of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is The chief adviser to the Prime Minister on matters of national security and strategic affairs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Security Advisor (NSA) is the chief adviser to the Prime Minister of India on matters of national security and strategic (foreign and defence) affairs. (राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा सलाहकार)

 

• The NSA is the senior official of the National Security Council (NSC) and advises the Prime Minister on internal and external security threats. The office is NOT a constitutional post; it was created by an executive order in 1998, and its first NSA was Brajesh Mishra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

 

• The National Security Council (NSC) is the apex body that looks after the political, economic, energy and security concerns of the nation; it is headed by the Prime Minister.

 

• Ajit Doval is one of the well-known holders of the office of NSA.

 

NOTE

 

• Because the NSA is an appointed adviser (an executive office), it is not a constitutional post and has no fixed constitutional tenure.

question: Which Indian athlete won the gold medal in the men's javelin throw at the 2023 World Athletics Championships?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neeraj Chopra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Neeraj Chopra won the gold medal in the men's javelin throw at the 2023 World Athletics Championships, held in Budapest, Hungary. This was India's first-ever gold medal at the World Athletics Championships. (नीरज चोपड़ा — विश्व एथलेटिक्स चैंपियनशिप 2023, स्वर्ण)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — Neeraj Chopra's achievements)

 

• Neeraj Chopra won India's first-ever Olympic gold medal in athletics at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics (in javelin throw).

 

• He later won a silver medal at the Paris 2024 Olympics.

 

• He hails from Haryana and is one of India's most celebrated athletes.

 

NOTE

 

• At the 2023 World Championships, another Indian, Kishore Jena, also performed well in the javelin throw and finished among the top competitors.

question: Article 356 of the Indian Constitution deals with which of the following?
option_1: The imposition of President's Rule in a State (State Emergency)
option_4: The establishment of the Finance Commission
solution_text:
The correct answer is The imposition of President's Rule in a State (State Emergency).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 356 of the Constitution deals with the imposition of President's Rule (also called State Emergency or 'constitutional emergency') in a State, in case of the failure of the constitutional machinery in that State. (अनुच्छेद 356 — राष्ट्रपति शासन)

 

• Under President's Rule, the President can assume the functions of the State government, and the powers of the State Legislature are exercised by the Parliament.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — types of emergency)

 

• Article 352 - National Emergency (due to war, external aggression or armed rebellion).

 

• Article 356 - President's Rule / State Emergency (failure of constitutional machinery in a State).

 

• Article 360 - Financial Emergency (threat to the financial stability of India).

 

NOTE

 

• The Supreme Court, in the S. R. Bommai case (1994), laid down guidelines to prevent the misuse of Article 356 and made the proclamation of President's Rule subject to judicial review.

question:
Consider the following statements about light:

1. The speed of light in vacuum is about 3 x 10^8 metres per second.

2. Light travels faster in water than in vacuum.

3. White light can be split into seven colours by a glass prism (a process called dispersion).

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: The speed of light in vacuum is about 3 x 10^8 metres per second (approximately 3,00,000 km per second) - the maximum possible speed in nature.

 

• Statement 2 is INCORRECT: Light travels SLOWER in water (and other denser media) than in vacuum. Light travels fastest in vacuum; when it enters a denser medium such as water or glass, its speed decreases.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: When white light passes through a glass prism, it splits into its seven constituent colours (VIBGYOR - violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red). This phenomenon is called 'dispersion'.

 

• Hence, only statements 1 and 3 are correct. (प्रकाश)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

 

• The splitting of white light by a prism was first demonstrated by Sir Isaac Newton.

 

• A rainbow is formed by the dispersion of sunlight by tiny water droplets in the atmosphere.

 

NOTE

 

• Since statement 2 is false, the correct answer is 'Only 1 and 3'.

question:
Fill in the blank:

The ________ is a classical dance form of Odisha, characterised by the graceful 'tribhangi' posture and traditionally performed by 'maharis' in temples.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Odissi' is a classical dance form of Odisha. It is one of the oldest surviving classical dance forms of India and is characterised by the graceful, curved body postures such as the 'tribhangi' (the three-bend posture) and the 'chowk'. (ओडिसी — ओडिशा)

 

• It was traditionally performed by female temple dancers called 'maharis', and later also by young boys called 'gotipuas'. Its themes are largely devotional, based on the worship of Lord Jagannath and the Gita Govinda.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — the eight classical dances and their states)

 

• Bharatanatyam - Tamil Nadu

• Kathak - Uttar Pradesh (North India)

• Kathakali and Mohiniyattam - Kerala

• Kuchipudi - Andhra Pradesh

• Odissi - Odisha

• Manipuri - Manipur

• Sattriya - Assam

 

NOTE

 

• The 'tribhangi' (three-bend) posture, in which the body is bent at the neck, waist and knee, is a distinctive feature of the Odissi dance.

question: The 'Logistics Performance Index (LPI)', which ranks countries on their trade logistics performance, is published by which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The World Bank.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Logistics Performance Index (LPI) is published by the World Bank. It is an interactive benchmarking tool that ranks countries on their trade logistics performance. (लॉजिस्टिक्स परफॉर्मेंस इंडेक्स — विश्व बैंक)

 

• The LPI is based on factors such as the efficiency of customs, the quality of trade and transport infrastructure, the ease of arranging shipments, the quality of logistics services, and the timeliness of shipments. The 2023 edition also incorporated indicators using 'big data' to measure the speed of trade.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — reports by the World Bank and others)

 

• World Bank - Logistics Performance Index, World Development Report.

 

• World Economic Forum - Global Competitiveness Report, Global Gender Gap Report.

 

• India has launched initiatives such as the National Logistics Policy and the PM Gati Shakti master plan to improve its logistics performance.

 

NOTE

 

• The World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) are together known as the 'Bretton Woods institutions'.

question: The 'National Institute of Oceanography (NIO)', a leading research institute in India, has its headquarters in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Panaji (Goa).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Institute of Oceanography (NIO) has its headquarters in Panaji (Dona Paula), Goa. It is a leading research institute that carries out scientific research and studies related to the oceans. (राष्ट्रीय समुद्र विज्ञान संस्थान — गोवा)

 

• The NIO is one of the constituent laboratories of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR). It was established in 1966.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — some important research institutes)

 

• Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology (WIHG) - Dehradun (studies Himalayan geology and glaciers).

 

• Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) - Hyderabad.

 

• Zoological Survey of India (ZSI) - Kolkata.

 

• Botanical Survey of India (BSI) - Kolkata.

 

NOTE

question: Which layer of the Earth's atmosphere lies immediately above the troposphere and contains the ozone layer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The stratosphere.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'stratosphere' is the layer of the atmosphere that lies immediately above the troposphere. It contains the ozone layer, which absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation. (समताप मंडल — ओज़ोन परत)

 

• Because ozone absorbs UV rays, the temperature in the stratosphere increases with height. This stability makes the stratosphere ideal for jet aircraft to fly in.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — layers of the atmosphere, from the surface upwards)

 

• Troposphere - the lowest layer; all weather phenomena occur here.

 

• Stratosphere - contains the ozone layer.

 

• Mesosphere - the coldest layer; most meteors burn up here.

 

• Thermosphere - contains the ionosphere; temperature rises sharply.

 

• Exosphere - the outermost layer, merging into outer space.

 

NOTE

 

• The 'Karman line', at about 100 km above sea level, is generally taken as the boundary between the Earth's atmosphere and outer space.

question:
Consider the following statements:

Statement 1: Article 32 of the Constitution provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies.

Statement 2: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described Article 32 as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both Statement 1 and Statement 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. (अनुच्छेद 32)

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Article 32 of the Constitution provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies, which empowers citizens to move directly to the Supreme Court for the enforcement of their Fundamental Rights.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described Article 32 as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution, because it makes the Fundamental Rights meaningful by providing an effective remedy for their enforcement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented — Article 32)

 

• Under Article 32, the Supreme Court can issue five types of writs: habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto.

 

• The High Courts have similar (and even wider) writ powers under Article 226.

 

NOTE

 

• Both statements about Article 32 are correct, so the answer is 'Both Statement 1 and Statement 2'.
